conversation_summary.date: 2026-09-13 (fact-checked vs HuggingFace/Cognition/Sakana primary sources; GLM-5.2 Turbo deleted; V4.1 Flash fixed 552B/8B+16B/280GB/CED; SWE-2+Fugu Max+Fugu Ultra v2.0 added; Qwen3.8-Max-Preview retired; Nemotron 3.5 Lightning duplicate deduped)
conversation_summary.goal: Compare API costs versus local hardware for extremely high-volume agentic coding.

workload.loop: read -> plan -> edit -> run -> inspect -> test -> fix -> repeat

Tencent Hy3.note: CSV lists Hy3 as Free; local only

Qwen3 Coder Next.note: no price in CSV; estimate from conversation

key_points: At 1B tokens/day, recurring API costs become very large.
DeepSeek V4 Flash-0731 was identified as a strong price/performance option.
DeepSeek V4 Pro costs more but remains much cheaper than many frontier proprietary models.
Kimi K3 has very high capability but much higher API cost than cheaper open models.
Agentic coding can have very high repeated-context/cache-hit rates, which can radically change API cost.
At 1B total tokens/day with 99% input, average output generation needed is about 116 tokens/sec if evenly distributed.

cache_notes.note: Actual agentic billing depends on cache-hit rate, context construction, tool outputs and provider.

DeepSeek V4.1 Flash (GA Sep 10).note: api-docs.deepseek.com Sep 10: model deepseek-flash = V4.1 Flash; legacy deepseek-v4-flash/vision-exp retired+routed billed Flash; deepseek-v4-pro routed to V4.1 Flash Sep 14 12:00 Beijing until V4.1 Pro

DeepSeek V4 Flash (legacy, superseded).note: Legacy aliases retired; served by V4.1 Flash and billed at Flash price. Old flat $0.14/$0.28 and derived off-peak $0.21/$0.66 rows in CSV kept for history with (legacy) flags.

DeepSeek V4.1 Flash weights.note: HF deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash Sep 10: MIT license, 763B total (~tiny active), 48 shards ~510GB FP8, ~382GB Q4, KV-cache compression headline, vision. Vendor evals @1M ctx minimal: TB2.1 90.6 / DeepSWE v1.1 74.2 / GPQA-D 90.9 / HLE-tools 63.9.

local_hardware.recommended_vram: At least 192GB VRAM; more is preferable for KV cache, runtime overhead and concurrency.

preferred_build.cpu: Threadripper Pro or EPYC-class workstation CPU

consumer_gpu_alternative.note: Potentially workable but much harder because of PCIe lanes, power, cooling, physical space and GPU-to-GPU communication.

example_economics.DeepSeek_V4_Flash_uncached_api: roughly ₹49 lakh/year under the 99% input / 1% output assumption
example_economics.caveat: High cache-hit rates can make API substantially cheaper.

conversation_summary.conclusion: For sustained 1B-token/day agentic coding, local open-weight inference can make economic sense, especially with high utilization and uncached API traffic. A hybrid setup—local open models for routine work and frontier APIs for difficult reasoning/review—may be optimal.
